$description: Dark mode theme — 12-step scales inverted (1=darkest, 12=lightest) + shadcn HSL semantics + dark-mode brand alias overrides. Mirrors .dark in @nebutra/tokens/styles.css.

brand.$description: Dark-mode brand alias overrides. In dark mode the visible brand fills shift to lighter steps for AA contrast on dark surfaces.

primary.$description: Dark-mode brand primary — the identity blue lifted to nebutra-blue-400 so it stays visible on dark surfaces. This is the identity alias, not the functional fill: the dark solid fill is --blue-9 (#396ae2, white label 4.85:1). The two are deliberately separate now that the VI hex is no longer pinned into ramp slot 9.

accent.$description: Dark-mode brand accent — nebutra-cyan-400 (L* 87.1). The functional bright fill is --cyan-9 (#0bf1c3, L* 85.41), the same hex in both modes; dark ink for it is --cyan-contrast at 10.35:1.

info.$description: Dark-mode info color — equals dark brand-primary.

hairline.$description: Hairline override — more visible on dark background

faint.$description: Dark-mode faint overlay (6% white) — inverted from light

6.$description: subtle border — DERIVED: OKLab lerp step5 → step9 at t=0.25, chroma forced to 0. The achromatic result is deliberate and preserves the documented intent of color.nebutra-gray ('used where blue undertone clashes — primarily dark-mode borders, dividers, elevation hairlines'). What was broken was the LIGHTNESS: gray-900/800/700 are darker than the slate background tier they sit above, so the border read as a hole rather than a hairline.

7.$description: default border — DERIVED: OKLab lerp step5 → step9 at t=0.50, chroma 0.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED: OKLab lerp step5 → step9 at t=0.75, chroma 0.

5.$description: component background active — L* 32.46, C 0.118. Anchor for the derived border tier.

6.$description: subtle border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 23.5 L*) at t=0.25. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 38.25, C 0.136.

7.$description: default border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 23.5 L*) at t=0.50. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 44.21, C 0.155.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 23.5 L*) at t=0.75. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 50.01, C 0.173.

9.$description: solid fill — L* 55.92, C 0.191, hue 264.3. White label 4.85:1. Same value as the dark shadcn --primary, so light and dark both take their deep fill from one source. Chroma ceiling for dark is 0.190; this is 0.191.

10.$description: solid fill hover — L* 57.44, C 0.183. White label 4.53:1. The hover has to move UP in a dark ramp, which costs contrast, so the step is deliberately small (1.52 L*) to keep white above 4.5:1.

11.$description: secondary text — L* 74.01, C 0.106. 8.62:1 on step 1.

12.$description: primary text — L* 90.52, C 0.043. 15.08:1 on step 1.

contrast.$description: Label ink for the solid fill tier. Absolute value, identical in both modes. 4.85:1 on step 9, 4.53:1 on step 10.

5.$description: component background active — L* 40.88, C 0.050. Anchor for the derived border tier.

6.$description: subtle border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (span 44.5 L*) at t=0.25. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 52.12, C 0.079.

7.$description: default border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (span 44.5 L*) at t=0.50. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 63.04, C 0.107.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (span 44.5 L*) at t=0.75. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 74.30, C 0.136.

9.$description: solid fill — same bright value as light mode, the way Radix ships one hex for mint-9 in both modes: L* 85.41, C 0.164. Ink 10.35:1 against --cyan-contrast.

10.$description: solid fill hover — L* 88.53, C 0.145, 3.12 L* above step 9 (Radix mint dark moves up 4.60 L*). Ink 11.34:1.

11.$description: secondary text — L* 91.46, C 0.110. 15.68:1 on step 1.

12.$description: primary text — L* 94.54, C 0.070. 16.95:1 on step 1.

contrast.$description: Label ink for the bright fill tier. Absolute near-black, identical in both modes. 10.35:1 on step 9, 11.34:1 on step 10.

primary.$description: Dark-mode action blue, paired with the near-black --primary-foreground, not white. #396ae2 keeps the VI hue and sits at L*55.9 C0.191.

primary-foreground.$description: White, matching light mode and matching --blue-contrast. It was near-black (222 14% 9%) when --primary was a LIGHT fill at L* 68.3, where dark ink read 6.20:1. Once --primary became a deep fill at L* 55.9 the pairing inverted and measured 3.74:1, below AA — the fill moved and the ink did not. The deep-fill tier takes white in both modes; --blue-contrast says the same thing, and they must agree because --primary and --blue-9 are now the same value.

destructive-strong.$description: Red as FOREGROUND on a dark surface. --destructive (0 63% 38%) is 2.15:1 on --card here — a fill only. Lightened to 5.18:1 on --card / 5.61:1 on --neutral-1, which sits alongside the light-mode 5.42:1 so red reads with the same weight in both themes. Use --destructive for fills with --destructive-foreground on top; use this for red text and icons.

success-strong.$description: Green as foreground on a dark surface. Needs no adjustment — 142 60% 42% is already 4.83:1 as ink on its own 10% tint — so it deliberately equals --success, matching how --warning-strong behaves in this theme.

warning-strong.$description: Amber as foreground on a dark surface. Unlike light mode this needs no adjustment — 38 80% 52% is already 7.98:1 against --neutral-1 — so it deliberately equals --warning. The token exists in both themes so consumers can reference one name.

ring.$description: Focus ring (dark mode) — neutral light gray. Mirrors light-mode neutral foreground choice.

ambient-sm.$description: Ambient elevation, small. Contact layer plus a wide soft pool — the marketing-surface counterpart to the tight xs..2xl product ramp.

ambient-md.$description: Ambient elevation, medium. Default resting depth for a floating marketing card.

ambient-lg.$description: Ambient elevation, large. One step up from md; use for hover of a md surface, not as a resting default.

glass-sm.$description: Ambient-sm plus a lit top edge, for translucent panels over a blurred backdrop.

glass-md.$description: Ambient-md plus a lit top edge.

glass-lg.$description: Ambient-lg plus a lit top edge.

sheen.$description: Top-edge sheen for solid inverted fills (bg-foreground). Lifts with light on a dark fill, with shade on a light one.

ambient-glow.$description: Centred offsetless halo — the only non-directional step on the ramp. Inverted from the light value: a black halo has nothing to darken against a dark surround, so the halo becomes light. Keep the alpha low; this is separation, not a bloom.

glow-accent.$description: Identical to the light value by design. The pool is theme-invariant black because glow-accent surfaces are fixed dark glass in both themes; only the accent halo shifts, via --brand-accent.

glow-accent-lg.$description: Hover escalation of glow-accent. Identical to the light value by design.

glow-accent-sm.$description: Accent halo alone, no pool. Identical to the light value by design.

glow-primary.$description: xl geometry tinted with the action fill at 5 percent. Same reference as light; --primary carries the dark channels.
